summary: Sevabertinib (Hyrnuo) is an oral selective HER2 (ERBB2) tyrosine kinase inhibitor granted accelerated approval for adults with locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC harboring HER2 tyrosine kinase domain activating mutations detected by an FDA-authorized test, covering both previously treated disease and first-line use (expanded September 9, 2026). Approval was based on the single-arm SOHO-01 trial. The recommended dose is 20 mg orally twice daily with food until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Key risks include severe diarrhea with dehydration and electrolyte imbalance, hepatotoxicity, left ventricular ejection fraction decrease, QT prolongation risk, interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis, and embryo-fetal toxicity.
indications: Treatment of adults with locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring HER2 (ERBB2) tyrosine kinase domain activating mutations, as detected by an FDA-authorized test, including after prior systemic therapy and as first-line treatment (accelerated approvals)

moa: Sevabertinib (Hyrnuo) is an oral small-molecule kinase inhibitor selective for HER2 (ERBB2) tyrosine kinase domain activating mutations. By occupying the ATP-binding pocket of mutant HER2, it blocks receptor autophosphorylation and downstream signaling through the MAPK and PI3K/AKT pathways, inhibiting tumor cell proliferation and survival in HER2-mutant non-squamous NSCLC.

absolute: Known serious hypersensitivity to sevabertinib or any excipient
monitor: Stool frequency, hydration, and electrolytes for severe diarrhea
Left ventricular ejection fraction and ECG for cardiac effects (LVEF decrease, QT risk)
New or worsening respiratory symptoms for interstitial lung disease
relative: History or risk of QT prolongation or cardiac dysfunction
Prior or active interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis
Moderate to severe hepatic impairment (limited data)

preg: Based on its mechanism of action and animal findings, sevabertinib can cause fetal harm. Verify pregnancy status before starting in females of reproductive potential and advise effective contraception during treatment and after the last dose per prescribing information.
lact: There are no data on the presence of sevabertinib in human milk or its effects on the breastfed child or milk production. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and after the final dose per prescribing information.
renal: No established dose adjustment in renal impairment. Monitor closely in moderate to severe impairment and for dehydration secondary to severe diarrhea.
hepatic: Monitor liver tests before and during treatment. Withhold, reduce, or discontinue for hepatotoxicity per prescribing information; limited data in moderate to severe hepatic impairment.

interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction is described; limit alcohol due to additive gastrointestinal and hepatic effects.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor liver tests, electrolytes (diarrhea-related losses), ECG, and left ventricular ejection fraction; evaluate respiratory symptoms with imaging if interstitial lung disease is suspected.
interactions.food: Take with food; swallow tablets whole.
major: QT-prolonging drugs - additive risk of QT prolongation and arrhythmia; avoid or monitor ECG closely
Strong CYP3A inducers - may reduce sevabertinib exposure; avoid where possible
minor: Acid-reducing agents and other minor interactions per full prescribing information; review concomitant medicines.
moderate: Other hepatotoxic agents - additive liver injury risk; monitor liver tests
Drugs that lower potassium or magnesium (diuretics) - worsen QT and arrhythmia risk; correct electrolytes
Other agents associated with pneumonitis - additive lung toxicity

pearls: Selective HER2 TKI for HER2 TKD-mutant non-squamous NSCLC; requires an FDA-authorized mutation test before treatment
Dosed 20 mg twice daily with food (not once daily), based on the SOHO-01 trial population
Severe diarrhea can cause dehydration and electrolyte loss; early antidiarrheal therapy plus dose holds are key
Cardiac vigilance: monitor LVEF and ECG; correct potassium and magnesium
Embryo-fetal toxicity: verify pregnancy status and require effective contraception
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember unless it is close to the next scheduled dose. Skip the missed dose in that case and resume the regular schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: There is no specific antidote for sevabertinib overdose. Manage with supportive care and monitor for exaggerated toxicities including severe diarrhea with dehydration and electrolyte imbalance, hepatotoxicity, and cardiac effects. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
